claims.text: Increasing Cr content in CrMnFeCoNi promotes selective oxidation.
Cr enrichment preferentially produces a Cr2O3-rich oxide scale.
The Cr-enriched alloy forms a more continuous oxide layer than the equiatomic baseline.
The Cr-enriched alloy forms a more adherent oxide layer than the equiatomic baseline.
A continuous Cr2O3-rich scale retards oxygen ingress.
Retarding oxygen ingress through the Cr2O3-rich scale enhances oxidation resistance.
Cr has sufficiently high oxygen affinity to drive the proposed selective oxidation.
Controlled Cr diffusion in the high-entropy matrix causes Cr to segregate to the surface.
Surface-segregated Cr forms a compact Cr2O3-rich barrier.
High configurational disorder in the alloy promotes defect repair within the oxide.
Disorder-assisted defect repair stabilizes the oxide scale and further limits oxygen penetration.
The Cr-enriched alloy will exhibit lower oxidation weight gain than the equiatomic baseline.
The Cr-enriched alloy will exhibit parabolic oxidation kinetics at 1000°C.
The baseline alloy is expected to form a mixed and spatially nonuniform oxide scale.
The baseline alloy is expected to have a higher oxidation rate than the Cr-enriched alloy.
CrTaO4 could become a dominant competing oxide in the specified CrMnFeCoNi alloys.
The proposed hypothesis is bounded to oxidation in air near 1000°C for durations up to 200 hours.
Failure of the Cr-enriched alloy to show both a lower oxidation rate and a predominantly continuous Cr2O3-rich scale relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The specified alloys contain only Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, and Ni, yet CrTaO4 is treated as a plausible competing phase and falsifier. Formation of CrTaO4 requires Ta, which is not included in either stated composition.
